THOUGHT: A 43-year-old woman with abnormal vaginal bleeding had D&C; tumor tissue showed loss of MSH6 protein by immunohistochemistry, MSI testing was negative, and a pathogenic germline MSH6 truncating mutation (R1331X) was identified. Loss of MSH6 on IHC plus a germline MSH6 mutation strongly points to a mismatch‑repair–deficient tumor caused by Lynch syndrome. Endometrial carcinoma is the most common Lynch‑associated tumor in women and commonly presents with abnormal vaginal bleeding at a younger-than-sporadic age, so MSH6‑deficient endometrial adenocarcinoma is the leading diagnosis. MSI testing can be false‑negative or show low MSI in some MSH6‑mutant tumors, so a negative MSI does not exclude MMR deficiency when IHC and germline testing indicate MSH6 loss. Other possibilities include precursor lesions (atypical endometrial hyperplasia) or other uterine malignancies that present with bleeding (carcinosarcoma, serous carcinoma, uterine sarcoma), but these are less likely given the MSH6 findings and typical presentation.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Mismatch‑repair–deficient endometrial carcinoma (MSH6‑loss, Lynch syndrome–associated endometrioid adenocarcinoma)
2. Atypical endometrial hyperplasia / endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (MSH6‑deficient precursor lesion)
3. Uterine (endometrial) serous carcinoma (less likely but can present with bleeding)
4. Uterine carcinosarcoma (malignant mixed Müllerian tumor)
5. Uterine sarcoma (e.g., endometrial stromal sarcoma or leiomyosarcoma)
